newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LAST-MINUTE STRIKE KEEPS CHESTERFIELD HOPES ALIVE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LAST-MINUTE STRIKE KEEPS CHESTERFIELD HOPES ALIVE.

text.p: Tiny Chesterfield kept their F.A. Cup dreams alive when they scored in the last minute of extra-time to earn a 3-3 draw with premier league Middlesbrough in an astonishing semifinal on Sunday.

Right-back Jamie Hewitt scored the dramatic equaliser for the second divison side with seconds remaining after 10-man Middlesbrough had first fought back from 2-0 down to force extra time and then taken a 3-2 lead in the 100th minute through Italian Gianluca Festa.
Hewitt scored with a header to rekindle Chesterfield's hopes of becoming the first team from outside the top two English divisions to reach the final.

As the ball looped into the net, the blue half of the 50,000-strong crowd at neutral Old Trafford went wild and Middlesbrough's foreign heroes Juninho and Fabrizio Ravanelli sank to their knees in despair.
For Middlesbrough the outcome was depressingly similar to the League Cup final against Leicester a week ago, when they conceded a 118th minute goal and had to settle for a 1-1 draw.
They face a replay of that match on Wednesday night at Sheffield's Hillsborough before tackling Chesterfield again at the same stadium on April 22.

The first turning point in Sunday's extraordinary match came in the 37th minute when Slovakian defender Vladimir Kinder, who had earlier been booked, was sent off for tugging back Kevin Davies on the edge of the box.

Chesterfield took advantage of the extra man early in the second half, taking the lead through Andy Morris, who stole in at the back post to fire home from close range after Davies' initial shot had been deflected across the Middlesbrough penalty area.
Seven minutes later the Derbyshire side, playing in their first ever F.A. Cup semifinal, extended their lead from the penalty spot.
Morris bustled his way into the box and was pulled down by Boro's stand-in keeper Ben Roberts, who was lucky to escape with just a booking.
Chesterfield captain Sean Dyche cracked home the spot-kick and one of the greatest F.A. Cup upsets in history appeared to be a probability rather than a slim possibility.
But three minutes later Italian Fabrizio Ravanelli met a Clayton Blackmore cross and bundled the ball into the back of the net to make the score 2-1 and give Boro hope.

Chesterfield then appeared to have a perfectly good goal disallowed. Striker Jonathan Howard crashed a shot off the underside of the crossbar and it seemed to cross the line before bouncing back into play.
But referee David Elleray ruled against the second division side and within three minutes Boro drew level with the second penalty of the match.

Dyche, who was otherwise oustanding in the Chesterfield back four, was adjudged to have barged Juninho off the ball, Craig Hignett made no mistake from the spot and the match moved into extra time with both sides clearly wilting.
Boro took the lead for the first time in the match on 100 minutes when Italy's Gianluca Festa crashed home a rebound after defender Steve Vickers had struck the crossbar with a fierce drive.
But before his side could celebrate their first appearance in an F.A. Cup final after 121 years of trying, Hewitt stole Chesterfield's deserved equaliser.
Middlesbrough manager Bryan Robson, clearly disappointed at his side's late capitulation, said the turning point in the match was the early dismissal of Kinder.
"I don't think the referee was right to book him and he was just waiting to get his red card out of his pocket after the second challenge," he said.
"Chesterfield worked very hard and made it difficult for us, but the referee made it more difficult."
An emotional Chesterfield boss John Duncan, who was applauded into his post-match news conference, described the match as the high point of his career.
"To score three goals against Middlesbrough is something I just didn't expect. I thought it would be backs to the wall for us and that we'd have to try and get a goal on the break.
"I'm just glad to have another chance."
